entity.name: Vladimir Putin
entity.description: The KGB spy who became Russia's modern tsar. A former intelligence officer in Dresden who rose through Saint Petersburg politics to seize the Russian presidency in 2000, Putin has ruled as an increasingly authoritarian leader for over two decades, launching wars in Chechnya, Georgia, and Ukraine.

story.name: Vladimir Putin
story.description: KGB posting in Dresden, rapid rise through Yeltsin's Kremlin, annexation of Crimea, and full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The biography of Russia's longest-serving leader since Stalin.

moments.name: Vladimir Putin Is Born in Post-Siege Leningrad
moments.subtitle: His two older brothers had already died — one of diphtheria during the Nazi blockade
moments.description: On October 7, 1952, Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin was born in Leningrad (now Saint Petersburg), the youngest of three children. His two older brothers had both died before his birth — one in infancy in the 1930s and the other of diphtheria during the devastating 872-day Siege of Leningrad in 1942, which killed over a million civilians. Putin's father had been severely wounded in World War II; his mother survived as a factory worker. The family lived in a communal apartment in a city still scarred by war. Putin would later invoke his family's wartime suffering as a defining element of his political identity.

moments.name: A KGB Officer Named Putin Spies in Dresden for Five Years
moments.subtitle: Officially a translator, he liaised with the Stasi and burned files as the Wall fell
moments.description: From 1985 to 1990, Vladimir Putin served as a KGB officer in Dresden, East Germany, under cover as a translator. Putin liaised with the Stasi secret police and was promoted to lieutenant colonel. When the Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, Putin famously confronted anti-communist protesters outside the KGB villa and frantically burned classified documents — so many that the furnace burst. The five years in Dresden shaped Putin's worldview: he witnessed the collapse of Soviet power firsthand and later described the fall of the USSR as the greatest geopolitical catastrophe of the 20th century.

moments.name: Boris Yeltsin Resigns and Hands Russia to Vladimir Putin
moments.subtitle: A virtually unknown ex-spy becomes acting president on New Year's Eve
moments.description: On December 31, 1999, Russian President Boris Yeltsin stunned the world by announcing his resignation on live television, effective immediately. Vladimir Putin, who had been appointed prime minister only four months earlier in August 1999, became acting president of Russia. Putin was largely unknown to the Russian public — he had risen from obscurity through Saint Petersburg municipal politics to the directorship of the FSB security service in just a few years. Less than three months later, on March 26, 2000, Putin won the presidential election. His rapid ascent from anonymous bureaucrat to head of state remains one of the most dramatic political rises of the modern era.

moments.name: Russia Annexes Crimea from Ukraine Without a Formal War
moments.subtitle: Soldiers without insignia seize the peninsula in weeks, triggering international sanctions
moments.description: In February–March 2014, Russian forces without military insignia — dubbed "little green men" — seized key sites across Crimea following the ouster of Ukraine's pro-Russian president. On March 16, a hastily organized referendum reported 97% support for joining Russia, widely dismissed by Western governments as illegitimate. On March 18, Putin signed a treaty formally annexing Crimea into the Russian Federation, the first forcible annexation of European territory since World War II. The act triggered sweeping international sanctions and a war in eastern Ukraine. The annexation fundamentally reshaped European security and foreshadowed the full-scale invasion eight years later.

moments.name: Russia Launches a Full-Scale Invasion of Ukraine
moments.subtitle: The largest military attack on a European state since 1945 begins before dawn
moments.description: On February 24, 2022, Russia launched a full-scale military invasion of Ukraine, striking cities across the country with missiles and sending ground forces toward Kyiv from multiple directions. Vladimir Putin announced the operation on television, calling it a "special military operation." The invasion prompted unprecedented international sanctions, the largest refugee crisis in Europe since World War II, and a united Western response including massive military aid to Ukraine. In March 2023, the International Criminal Court issued an arrest warrant for Putin for war crimes related to the forced deportation of Ukrainian children.
